quick_facts.label: What the job is
quick_facts.value: Industrial engineers design, develop, test and evaluate integrated systems for managing industrial production processes, including quality control, inventory, logistics and material flow, and cost analysis.

quick_facts.label: Other names for it
quick_facts.value: Job titles O*NET reports for this occupation (Industrial Engineers) include Industrial Engineer, Continuous Improvement Engineer, Operations Engineer and Process Engineer.

quick_facts.label: Typical preparation
quick_facts.value: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Four (considerable preparation needed): most of these occupations require a four-year bachelor's degree, but some do not.

sections.heading: What an industrial engineer does
paragraphs: Industrial engineers design, develop, test and evaluate integrated systems for managing industrial production processes, including quality control, inventory, logistics and material flow, and cost analysis.

The tasks below are taken from the O*NET profile for Industrial Engineers. O*NET is the US Department of Labor's occupation database, so this describes the job as it is profiled in the United States; titles and duties in Indian companies can differ.
bullets: Estimate production costs and the effect of product design changes on spending.
Plan the sequence of operations used to make and assemble parts or products.
Analyse statistical data and specifications to set quality and reliability objectives.
Work with management and users to develop production and design standards.

sections.heading: How people get into this job
paragraphs: O*NET places this occupation in Job Zone Four (considerable preparation needed): most of these occupations require a four-year bachelor's degree, but some do not.
In India, the UGC specification of degrees lists B.Tech and B.E. as four-year bachelor's degrees entered after 10+2.
